import pandas as pd

def load_source_data(file_paths):
    """
    Load multiple CSV files into a single DataFrame by concatenation.
    Assumes all source files have the same schema.
    """
    dfs = []
    for path in file_paths:
        df = pd.read_csv(path)
        dfs.append(df)
    combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)
    return combined_df

def transform_data(df):
    """
    Transform the combined source DataFrame to match the target schema and types.
    The source schema matches the target schema exactly, so minimal transformation is needed.
    This function ensures correct data types and handles any missing values if necessary.
    """
    # Define the target schema with expected types
    # Note: categories and tags can be string or list-like strings, keep as is (string)
    # Booleans: completed, deleted, mature
    # Integers: commentCount, copyright, firstPartId, firstPublishedPart.id, id, language.id,
    # lastPublishedPart.id, length, numParts, rating, readCount, voteCount
    # Strings: all others
    
    # Convert boolean columns explicitly
    bool_cols = ['completed', 'deleted', 'mature']
    for col in bool_cols:
        # Some CSVs might have these as bool or int or string, normalize to bool
        df[col] = df[col].map(lambda x: True if str(x).lower() in ['true', '1'] else False)
    
    # Convert integer columns explicitly
    int_cols = ['commentCount', 'copyright', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.id', 'id',
                'language.id', 'lastPublishedPart.id', 'length', 'numParts', 'rating', 'readCount', 'voteCount']
    for col in int_cols:
        df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)
    
    # For string columns, ensure they are strings (including timestamps)
    str_cols = ['categories', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp', 'createDate', 'description',
                'firstPublishedPart.createDate', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate',
                'modifyDate', 'parts', 'tags', 'title', 'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name']
    for col in str_cols:
        # Some columns might have NaN, convert to empty string
        df[col] = df[col].fillna('').astype(str)
    
    # Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
    target_columns = ['categories', 'commentCount', 'completed', 'copyright', 'cover', 'cover_timestamp',
                      'createDate', 'deleted', 'description', 'firstPartId', 'firstPublishedPart.createDate',
                      'firstPublishedPart.id', 'id', 'language.id', 'language.name', 'lastPublishedPart.createDate',
                      'lastPublishedPart.id', 'length', 'mature', 'modifyDate', 'numParts', 'parts', 'rating',
                      'readCount', 'tags', 'title', 'url', 'user.avatar', 'user.fullname', 'user.name', 'voteCount']
    
    df = df[target_columns]
    
    return df

def main():
    # List all source CSV file paths
    source_files = [
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_0.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_1.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_2.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_3.csv",
        "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_30/test_4.csv"
    ]
    
    # Load all source data
    combined_df = load_source_data(source_files)
    
    # Transform data to target schema and types
    transformed_df = transform_data(combined_df)
